result.notes:
Overall US-6 verdict: all three ACs SATISFIED, independently re-verified (not merely re-read from DRILL_EVIDENCE.md).

Key independent evidence produced during verification:
- Re-executed execution-report.js on RELOCATED COPIES of jobs 0001/0002/0006 and got byte-for-byte identical verdicts/exit codes (only generated_at differs), proving AC-6.1's pure-from-files claim and reproducing the AC-6.2 live matrix cells.
- Ran the script on the committed fixtures and the fixture harness (run-tests.js → 8/8 + CLI-error PASS) to confirm exit 0 (clean PROMOTE) and exit 2 (QUARANTINE).
- Programmatic AC-6.3 check: ALL_TRACEABLE=true, 0 misses.

Live-vs-fixture split for AC-6.2 (per instruction to enumerate explicitly):
- LIVE drills: promote-with-warn exit 10 (job_0001), retry exit 1 (job_0002 PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED, job_0006 BUILD_GATE_FAILURE).
- FIXTURE ONLY (committed deterministic, NOT live demonstrations): clean-PROMOTE exit 0 (promote_clean) and QUARANTINE exit 2 (quarantine / quarantine_grader_fail / quarantine_drift_block).
This split matches DRILL_EVIDENCE.md's own enumeration and is legitimate: exit-code semantics are a reproducibility/correctness property for which deterministic fixtures are valid evidence, and the exit constants match the ADWS_Pro original exactly.

Caveat (non-blocking, does not change any AC verdict): finding F-1 — adws-planner emits `file_change_proposal[].reason` while repo-context-scan.js checks `p.description`, so every well-formed live plan trips a spurious build `warn`, forcing real jobs to land as PROMOTE-with-warnings (exit 10) rather than clean PROMOTE (exit 0). This is why the exit-0 cell of the verdict matrix could not be reproduced by a live drill and relies on the committed fixture. F-1 is a producer/assembler-side defect flagged for wrap-up; it does not affect the correctness of the execution-report script or any US-6 AC.

Scope note: US-6 ACs are about the report/verdict machinery. I did not re-verify upstream drill claims owned by other user stories (e.g. live PR URL for US-5, worktree isolation for FR-8, consensus independence for US-4) beyond confirming the evidence files they wrote are present and traceable.

result.notes:
Both US-4 ACs verified satisfied against real artifacts, code, and specs.

Caveats and observations for sign-off:
1) AC-4.1 rests on live-drill artifacts (job_0001) that are gitignored/local-only; I independently confirmed the four consensus files exist with independent role-tagged verdicts and that the orchestration spec + agent contracts require separate fresh-context parallel dispatch with only contract+changeset. I cannot replay the actual subagent invocations, so 'separate subagents' is established by artifact consistency + spec, not by re-observing the dispatch.
2) AC-4.2's blocking/verbatim-surfacing behavior is proven by the committed deterministic fixture (parity/execution-report-fixtures/quarantine) executed live through execution-report.js (exit 2 = QUARANTINE, dissent rendered verbatim in two places). No real Advocate dissent occurred in any live drill, so this AC is validated at the RULE + report-code level, as the task itself scoped.
3) Minor, non-blocking schema drift in the live evidence (does not affect either verdict): the live critic.json 'findings' is a string, whereas adws-critic.md's template shows an array of {issue,evidence}; and review/attempt_1/consensus/advocate.json omits the 'findings' key entirely. Verdict/role/dissent fields (the AC-load-bearing ones) are present and independent in all four files. execution-report.js reads dissent defensively (typeof === 'string' guards, l.170-171), so this drift does not break dissent surfacing.
4) Consistency check: both live consensus roles recorded model_tier=haiku, matching the phase-gates.md low-risk tier table (Critic haiku / Advocate haiku); the agents' default frontmatter (critic:sonnet, advocate:haiku) is overridden by the orchestrator's per-FR-12 tier selection, which is expected, not a contradiction.

criteria.ac: AC-2.3: Phase order violations are impossible by procedure (no instruction path skips a gate).
criteria.proof: Instruction inspection: SKILL.md Hard rule 1 (lines 24-25): 'Phase order is plan -> build -> test -> review -> document -> ship -> verify. Never skip a phase; never start a phase while an earlier gate is failing.' SKILL.md Procedure section 2 gate-decision (lines 86-98) enumerates the ONLY outcomes: Pass -> proceed to next phase; Fail+retries -> new attempt of the SAME phase; test code-defect -> rewind BACKWARD to build; Fail+budget exhausted -> terminate. No branch advances past a failing gate or jumps ahead a phase. phase-gates.md lines 6-11 restate 'No phase may be skipped. No later phase may start while an earlier gate is failing' and gate rules 31-41 (pass->advance, fail+exhausted->terminate); cross-phase rewinds (43-54) are backward moves to build only. Deterministic backstop: execution-report.js:185-218 pipeline_completion gate FAILS unless all 7 PHASE_NAMES (line 40 = plan,build,test,review,document,ship,verify) produced an attempt AND final_status=='completed' — demonstrated LIVE in job_0006 execution_report.json: pipeline_completion result="fail", detail='2/7 — Missing phase outputs: test, review, document, ship, verify'. Thus a run that skipped phases cannot receive a clean PROMOTE; the report deterministically catches it.
criteria.method: Procedure/instruction inspection of SKILL.md and references/phase-gates.md (read in full) plus source inspection of execution-report.js pipeline_completion gate, AND a live demonstration of the backstop (job_0006 report shows pipeline_completion=fail 2/7). Honest caveat: enforcement is instruction-level + a post-hoc deterministic report backstop, NOT a hard runtime code lock preventing an orchestrator from emitting a wrong action mid-run — DPPD R-1 explicitly acknowledges 'Instruction-based gate enforcement is weaker than code enforcement.' The AC is scoped 'by procedure (no instruction path skips a gate)', which is met: I found no instruction path that permits skipping, and the pipeline_completion gate provides deterministic detection of any deviation.

result:
I have enough to render a completeness verdict. Here is my adversarial assessment.

---

## Completeness critic — findings

### (1) Coverage of DPPD §4: complete
All 16 section-4 acceptance criteria (AC-1.1→1.3, 2.1→2.3, 3.1→3.3, 4.1→4.2, 5.1→5.3, 6.1→6.3) appear in the per-story verdicts. **No section-4 AC is uncovered.** One scope note: DPPD §1.3 success criterion says "All **10** ported validators produce verdicts identical to the originals," but AC-3.1 (and the parity run) test only the **9** deterministic ones; the 10th (`pr.drift_sentinel.spec` / grader) is LLM-graded and has no parity test. That is inherent, not a gap, but the §1.3 "10" vs §4 "9" wording should be reconciled in sign-off so nobody reads AC-3.1's 79/79 as covering the grader.

### (2) Satisfied-on-weak/fixture evidence where a live demo was expected
Three ACs are marked satisfied without the live demonstration a reader would expect. All three are disclosed by the individual verifiers, and all are defensible for rule/reproducibility ACs — but they should be recorded as **conditional/fixture-backed**, not as live E2E passes:

- **AC-1.2 (vague task → ask, don't guess):** documentation-only. No vague task was ever submitted in any drill; the verdict rests entirely on the written rule in `task-contract.md:93-108`. This is a behavioral AC with a testable negative path (submit a task with no verifiable outcome, confirm the skill asks) that simply was not exercised. Weakest evidence in the set.
- **AC-4.2 (advocate dissent blocks promotion):** fixture-only. Every live drill produced unanimous pass (the trivial multiply task), so the block-and-quarantine path is shown only via the committed `execution-report-fixtures/quarantine` fixture run through the report script. The *code path* is proven; the *live behavior* is not.
- **AC-6.2 (verdict matrix):** only 2 of 4 cells are live (exit 10 promote-with-warn, exit 1 retry). Clean-PROMOTE (exit 0) and QUARANTINE (exit 2) are fixture-only. The exit-0 cell is **not merely undemonstrated — it is unreachable live** because of F-1 (below). That is the important one: a fixture is masking a real defect, not just standing in for an untriggered path.

### (3) Inconsistency between verifier claims and the artifacts
The most serious completeness problem is a mismatch between the DRILL_EVIDENCE.md header — *"All phase agents … were dispatched live as real subagents"* — and what the artifacts actually record about the **agent** phases (as opposed to the scripts and git side-effects):

- **Every `phase_manifest.json` in all 6 jobs — including flagship "fully live" job_0001 — records `model_used=null`, `cost_usd=null`, `token_count=null`.** There is no invocation telemetry anywhere tying any planner/builder/reviewer/tester run to an actual model call.
- **Timestamps are placeholders and in one case physically impossible:** job_0001 `build/attempt_1` `started_at=2026-07-15T00:47:00Z` — ~7 hours *before* its own `plan/attempt_1` at `07:46:25Z` (build before plan); job_0001 grader `graded_at=2026-07-15T00:00:00Z` (midnight placeholder); job_0006's committed `execution_report` `generated_at` predates the run's `started_at`.
- The US-4 consensus artifacts have **no** independence telemetry: `advocate.json` even omits the `findings` field entirely while `critic.json` carries a prose string, both stamped the same `assessed_at` to the minute. AC-4.1 "separate subagents, fresh context" is established by spec + artifact presence only.

What is genuinely, independently live-verifiable is narrower than the header implies and holds up well: the **git/gh state** (PR #1 OPEN at head `94c5986` = ship `commit_sha`; remote carries only `main`, `job_0001/multiply`, `job_0004/power`; job_0002/0003 provably never pushed) and the **deterministic scripts** (I reproduced exit 10/1/1 for jobs 0001/0002/0006 myself; parity 79/79). So US-5, US-3, and US-6's script machinery are solidly live. US-2's rewind and US-4's independent consensus rest on side-effect artifacts + spec, **not** on any evidence that a live LLM actually did the reasoning. Each verifier flagged the timestamp weirdness in isolation; none reconciled it against the blanket "dispatched live" claim. My recommendation: relabel the header as "orchestrated per SKILL.md; git/gh effects and validator/report outputs are live and reproducible; per-phase model telemetry was not captured" so the sign-off record isn't overclaiming the agentic path.

(Note: null `model_used`/`cost` on the *validator* `skill_trace.json` files is correct and expected — they're non-LLM scripts. The problem is the null telemetry on the *phase* manifests, which represent the LLM agents.)

### (4) F-1 and other defects — does anything block sign-off?
**F-1 is confirmed real, in code, and I verified both sides:**
- `repo-context-scan.js:60` gates on `p.description` (`proposals.some(p => !p.description || p.description.length < 3)` → `warn`).
- `adws-planner.md:19` specifies the planner emits `file_change_proposal: [{ file_path, action, reason }]` — **`reason`, never `description`.**

So every well-formed real plan trips the build-gate `warn`. Consequence, confirmed by re-running the report on job_0001: **every valid live job lands as PROMOTE-with-warnings (exit 10); clean PROMOTE (exit 0) is unreachable on any real run.** This is more than cosmetic — it is a producer/validator contract mismatch that degrades the verdict of *every* live job and is the sole reason AC-6.2's exit-0 cell had to fall back to a fixture. It fails *safe* (toward warn, never toward a false clean pass), so it is not a safety hole and does not, in my judgment, block a **conditional** sign-off. But it should block an **unqualified** one: DPPD §1.3's "produces a … PROMOTE … report" is met, but a *clean* PROMOTE has never been and cannot currently be demonstrated live. F-1 must be fixed on the producer/assembler side (planner emits `description`, or the orchestrator maps `reason`→`description`) and one live job re-drilled to show a genuine exit-0 before the exit-0 cell can be called live-demonstrated.

No other new defect rises to blocking. Secondary items for the record: the stale `version: "1.0.0"` in skill traces vs shipped `2.1.0` (US-1's noted discrepancy — cosmetic); and the consensus-schema drift in US-4 (advocate missing `findings`) — the report reads dissent defensively so it doesn't break, but it signals the consensus artifacts are loosely templated.

**Bottom line:** Coverage is complete. US-3, US-5, and the US-6 report machinery are backed by solid independent live/reproducible evidence. Recommend **conditional sign-off** contingent on: (a) fixing F-1 and re-drilling one live clean-PROMOTE; (b) relabeling AC-1.2, AC-4.2, and the exit-0/exit-2 cells of AC-6.2 as fixture/spec-backed rather than live; and (c) correcting the DRILL_EVIDENCE.md "dispatched live as real subagents" claim to match the absence of any per-phase model/cost/timestamp telemetry (the agentic ACs — US-2 rewind, US-4 independence — are corroborated by side-effects and spec, not by live-invocation evidence).
